terms.gloss: in the presence of, before; in person, face to face
terms.grammar: adverb; and preposition with the ablative
terms.comment: As a preposition, before a person’s eyes (cōram patre); as an adverb, in person, face to face, as against by letter: Cicero ends letters with it.

terms.gloss: present, in person; mē praesente, in my presence
terms.grammar: participle of praesum, as an adjective; often in the ablative absolute
terms.comment: Latin puts the person in the ablative absolute where English uses the abstract noun: mē praesente, in my presence; the opposite is mē absente (see absence).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 5.8.5: dēsīderium praesentiae tuae (Lewis & Short)
Caes. B.G. 5.43.4: praesentia animī, presence of mind (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The noun is classical but less used than the two above. In praesentiā means “for the present, now” (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: we’ll deal with the rest face to face

phrases.latin: quid, cum cōram sumus et garrīmus quicquid in buccam?
phrases.english: and what about when we are together and chatter whatever comes into our heads?

phrases.latin: verba quis audēret cōram sene digna rubōre dīcere?
phrases.english: who would have dared to say words to make one blush in front of an old man?
I’d rather hear it from you in person
here I am, face to face with you
